content: 1. Individuals involved in data management for cost collection or public health research should possess expertise in these areas. Prior experience in managing data is highly advantageous. 2. Most countries will utilize an online tool for data collection. In such cases, the Principal Investigator (PI) must be proficient in using the online data collection system and capable of troubleshooting and resolving any issues that arise. 3. The PI is responsible for overseeing the development of the research protocol and obtaining ethical clearance. 4. The PI acts as a liaison for communication with external partners and stakeholders, including staff from the National Tuberculosis Program (NTP), public health services, local research institutions, and other government departments. 5. The PI manages funding for data collection and ensures that financial reports comply with national procedures. 6. The PI assembles a data collection team with the necessary expertise to design, implement, and analyze tuberculosis (TB) provider cost data. 7. The PI maintains regular communication with research assistants, supervises their work, and ensures the quality of the study's conduct. 8. The PI writes the final study report and ensures its dissemination to key stakeholders identified during the stakeholder analysis. 9. The PI collaborates with the NTP to disseminate results to stakeholders, including those in health and non-health sectors. 10. The PI establishes contact with facilities sampled for the study and facilitates the introduction of research assistants and key information providers within each facility. 11. The PI validates double-entered data files and ensures proper storage and backup of data. 12. The PI regularly checks validated data files for systematic errors and prepares the database for analysis and data entry screens. 13. The PI contributes to the analysis of results and ensures that study findings are translated into policy recommendations. 14. The PI coordinates the overall implementation of cost collection in the field, including planning fieldwork and required training, and preparing training materials. 15. The PI ensures quality assurance processes are implemented according to the protocol and supervises implementation in health facilities and laboratories. 16. The PI plans and coordinates data collection monitoring visits involving all partners. 17. The PI oversees the provision of supplies and materials required for the study and organizes the writing of activity and final reports. 18. The PI plans the detailed budget for cost collection and periodically reports fund utilization to funders. 19. The PI arranges pilot testing and its evaluation and liaises with local officials in healthcare facilities and laboratories during pre-cost collection visits and fieldwork. 20. The PI promptly reports any major issues in preparation, execution, or data management of the cost collection. Qualifications for the PI: At least five years of managerial experience in public health, preferably with costing or health economics experience. Strong managerial skills, including task delegation. Extensive knowledge of TB management and the context of data collection. Familiarity with laboratory and facility-based costing. Access to an organization with infrastructure to support facility-based costing in the field. Research Assistants: 1. Research assistants will be based at health facilities and laboratories for one week per facility to collect data on resources used in TB prevention, diagnosis, and care. 2. They should have strong social and communication skills and be thoroughly trained in costing techniques and data collection tools. 3. They must be capable of managing technology if an online data collection tool is used. 4. Research assistants will conduct interviews with TB providers while respecting privacy and confidentiality. 5. They will analyze client registers, financial records, pharmacy/laboratory records, and other TB-related documentation to extract required information. 6. They will enter, manage, and maintain economic data collected from the field. 7. They will participate in data cleaning and analysis with support from the PI. 8. They must promptly communicate any technical or managerial bottlenecks to the study coordinator. Qualifications for Research Assistants: Prior experience in cost collection is desirable. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word. Good knowledge of the Kenyan health system and fluency in the local language. Strong administrative and organizational skills. Well-developed social and communication skills, particularly with staff. Prior experience in public health research or facility-based costing fieldwork. Technical Advisory Group: 1. The technical advisory group advises the PI on all technical aspects of cost collection, including approval and acceptance processes. 2. It provides technical input in statistical, epidemiological, and health economics activities. 3. Collaboration with the group is substantial during protocol design and adaptation but ad-hoc during data collection. 4. Members may include international experts and perform activities on a part-time basis, with varying workloads depending on the survey phase. 5. The group supports the translation of results into policy recommendations and dissemination of findings. Data Collection Coordinator: 1. The data collection coordinator manages the day-to-day implementation of cost collection and supervises research assistants. 2. They establish contact with sampled facilities and facilitate the introduction of research assistants and key information providers. 3. They adapt training manuals and cost collection materials and prepare standard operating procedures. 4. They train research assistants before data collection and provide retraining if needed. 5. They monitor the operational implementation of the survey and ensure quality assurance processes are followed. 6. They plan and coordinate data collection monitoring visits and oversee the provision of supplies and materials. 7. They report any major problems in preparation, execution, or data management without delay. Qualifications for Data Collection Coordinator: At least three years of research experience in public health. Strong managerial and coordination skills. Knowledge of public health research, health economics, and TB. Expertise in fieldwork and experience in planning and conducting cost data collection. Data Manager: 1. The data manager is responsible for identifying quality data issues and managing data collected by research assistants. 2. They validate double-entered data files, ensure proper storage and backup, and check data files for systematic errors. 3. They prepare the database for analysis and contribute to result analysis. 4. They liaise regularly with the data collection coordinator and report any data management problems promptly. Qualifications for Data Manager: Proven experience in leading and motivating teams. Extensive experience in health facility-based costing or public health research. Experience in analyzing data to provide summary statistics. Proficiency in troubleshooting data collection problems, including identifying systematic and ad-hoc errors. Strong administrative skills, including maintaining adequate documentation for costing or public health research. Case Study Example: A peri-urban clinic in Nairobi was visited to understand its workflow and patient flow. The clinic is located on a dirt road with market stalls on either side. The main clinic is a brick and concrete structure with a covered outdoor waiting area. A small laboratory is housed in a shipping container with wide windows but no running water. Posters with health messages, staff lists, and diagnostic algorithms are displayed on the walls. Patients wait outside under a shelter to protect them from the sun.
